demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Global textile market recovery for FY2025-26 is described as cautious and fragile, with business sentiment, order intake and capacity utilization improving versus 2025 but still below long-term averages.
- Demand weakness, high raw material and energy costs, and geopolitical risks continue to weigh on industry margins, particularly for upstream segments.
- India's textile and apparel market is largely domestic-consumption driven (~80%), with the balance from exports; 'China+1' sourcing diversification is seen as an opportunity for Indian players to capture export share.
- Company-specific: revenue decline attributed to lower and irregular production at the Nalagarh manufacturing unit, its only operating facility.
- Real estate monetization of Bathinda and Ludhiana land is expected to provide incremental non-operating cash flows supporting deleveraging.

capex_expansion.body: No new capacity-addition or expansion project is disclosed. The narrative instead describes rationalization: manufacturing at Bathinda was discontinued in FY2023-24 and at Ludhiana (Focal Point) ceased in March 2025, with both sites now the subject of real estate monetization plans rather than capacity investment. Only the Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh facility remains operational.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management's FY2025-26 risk assessment flagged cotton and man-made fiber price volatility as a factor that can materially affect business outcomes.
- Flagged by management as a commercial/operational risk for the textile sector affecting margins.
- Identified as a risk area in the Company's FY2025-26 risk assessment.
- Structural industry risk noted by management; Indian manufacturers face intense competition from China, Vietnam and Bangladesh with lower capital costs and more integrated supply chains.
- Management flagged FX exposure on export realisations as a risk requiring natural hedging and treasury management.
- Accelerating regulatory and buyer requirements on sustainability, traceability and labour compliance were flagged; non-adherence can lead to loss of orders or market access.
- Only the Nalagarh (Himachal Pradesh) facility remains operational after Bathinda (FY2023-24) and Ludhiana (March 2025) manufacturing were discontinued, concentrating production risk in one site.
- The Chairman's message and MD&A note that liquidity constraints adversely impacted operational and financial performance during the year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen competitiveness and restore profitable growth through disciplined operational and financial measures.
- Sustained cost optimization, productivity enhancements, waste minimization and quality improvements across manufacturing and supply chain to deliver more cost-competitive products.
- Pursue targeted measures to reduce debt servicing costs and improve capital efficiency.
- Unlock value from real estate holdings in Bathinda and Ludhiana through phased monetization to support deleveraging and strategic investments.
- Balance short-term liquidity and cost control with investments in capability building and product differentiation.
